newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Wider loss at Vocaltec seen.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Wider loss at Vocaltec seen.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said it was widening its estimate for losses at Israel's Vocaltec for the second half of 1996 and all of 1997 but that it was holding to its Venture rating for the stock.

Analyst Theodor Kundtz said higher R&D and marketing expenses due to an accelerated product rollout schedule would widen Vocaltec's third-quarter loss to $0.15 per share from his earlier $0.01 target.
Vocaltec, an Israeli maker of software to transmit voice communications over the Internet, is due to announce quarterly results on October 30.
For full-year 1996, VocalTec will show a loss of $0.46 a share, up from Lehman's previous estimate of $0.34, Kundtz said. For full-year 1997, he projected a $0.14 loss, versus an earlier $0.04.

VocalTec's unveiling of its Internet Voice Mail package earlier this week was part of the company's "aggressive schedule for developing and launching of new products," Kundtz said. "As a result, we have revised our model to reflect the likelihood that R&D and sales and marketing expenses will be higher than expected."

Kundtz said VocalTec should maintain revenue targets. "We believe Release 4, the company's mainstay product, continues to show strong growth, despite the growing number of Internet phone products available on the market," he said.
